response.query: What econometric models and instruments best estimate voucher-induced price pass-through to market prices while accounting for seasonality and clustering?
response.answer: Fixed effects models and instrumental variables best estimate voucher-induced price pass-through, accounting for seasonality and clustering. Seasonal dummy variables and robust standard errors are essential.

results.title: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services Fee Schedule and ...
results.content: In the 2020 fee rule, DHS required separate filing fees when filing Form I-765, Application for Employment Authorization, and Form I-131, Application for Travel Document, concurrently with a Form I-485, Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status, or after USCIS accepts their Form I-485 and while it is still pending. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) proposes to adjust certain immigration and naturalization benefit request fees charged by U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS). Because USCIS is primarily fee-funded, it must ensure that it maintains a carryover balance to continue operating, and INA section 286(m), 8 U.S.C. 1356(m) authorizes DHS to set fees at a level to recover “the *full* costs” of providing “ *all”* “adjudication and naturalization services,” and “the administration of the fees collected.” (emphasis added.) This necessarily includes support costs such as physical overhead, information technology, management and oversight, human resources, national security vetting and investigations,[26]  accounting and budgeting, and legal, for example. For a quick reference of the immigration benefit requests that currently require biometric services with the initial submission, *see* USCIS, Form G-1055, Fee Schedule, available at *https://www.uscis.gov/​g-1055.*.
